message:
test(host): stop the dispatcher suite from reconfiguring the user's firewall

Test 1, docs 1. The test no longer starts a host unless asked to.

It starts a real GNLinkStream, which listens, which makes Windows ask the user about an
executable it has never seen -- a scratch copy under %TEMP% with a different path every run. A
prompt nobody answers becomes a Block rule. Between my runs and the reviewer's, eight rules were
left on this machine: two Allow and six Block, one per scratch directory.

That is a test changing the machine's configuration, which is not a thing a test may do quietly.
The user noticed before either of us did -- they asked twice why something kept requesting
firewall access and which session it was.

So it is opt-in now, behind REMOTE60_ALLOW_HOST_E2E=1, and a default run prints why it skipped
rather than exiting silently: a regression sweep should not lose coverage without saying so, and
it should not rewrite a firewall without saying so either. Verified: a bare run starts no process
and opens no port.

--bind-address 127.0.0.1 is not a way out. The reviewer checked -- other listeners bind the
wildcard address regardless, so the prompt comes anyway.

The eight rules that already exist are recorded as 0.0.21 and deliberately left alone. Removing
them needs elevation, which needs the user to agree first, and the reviewer will handle it. This
commit removes the cause, not the residue.

Two control characters got into that entry on the way in and are worth naming, since it is the
same hazard twice: a shell heredoc ate one backslash level, so Python read the Windows paths
temp\v2lab and temp\remote60_... as escapes and wrote a vertical tab and a carriage return into
the document. Repaired with chr(92), and the file is now checked for control characters rather
than eyeballed.
